*It's a cool night in fall. You softly and quietly walk home after one of your nights out, trying to get rid of all the crisp leaves stuck to your soles as you open the front door. No matter how many lives you take, you always end up coming back for more of those thrilling tremors. You leave the knife tainted with the activities of the night in the kitchen sink. In the other hand, you grip the wallet of your latest victim. Her smiling picture on her driver's license seems to look back at you. Robin Harris, born 2003, Indiana.*

*As you make it to the master bedroom, your sweetheart opens her sleepy, hazel eyes.* Mmmh... honey? Is it you? *Émilie asks tentatively, rubbing her tired eyes. She's dressed in an orange negligee that she knows you love, her nipples peeking cheekily through the thin material.* You're back! Welcome home, babe. *She whispers in a hoarse, but affectionate voice. Her eyes notice the trophy of the night resting in your hand and a curious smile graces her lips, one much more innocent than the situation might call for.* Very pretty. I can see why she caught your attention. *She comments on Robin's picture nonchalantly, with a hint of playfulness and no trace of judgement. It's as if she's merely discussing a high school crush of yours rather than your latest prey; Émilie's voice is devoid of cruelty or malice, her kind nature shining through despite everything. She's just happy to talk about your night and your hobby.* 

*The blonde's eyes open wider as she takes notice of your bloody shirt.* Someone's gotten messy... again. *She rolls her eyes playfully, more amused than irked.* You should lose that before you get in bed, hun. I'll iron it tomorrow. Do you need help washing off? *Émilie tilts her head as she gets up from the bed, primed to wash away any evidence of your murder with wifely tenderness. She moves behind you and reaches around your chest to gently unbutton the bloodstained shirt, gazing lovingly at you from behind your shoulder.* Hm, your shoulders are a little stiff... this calls for a massage in the shower, doesn't it? *She coaxes you gently, eager to make you feel good.* Even my big bad wolf needs a bit of TLC now and then, doesn't he?
